bull_bear.body: Cash balance INR 853cr; Dividend INR 75/share declared; Greenfield project (est. INR 130cr total, land done) under evaluation based on demand traction; No M&A announced.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Morbi gas supply normalization reducing Cera's relative advantage; Delay in trade discount rationalization; Brass/clay cost volatility exceeding price hikes; Tiles segment disruption due to outsourcing reliance on Morbi; Wage code settlement uncertainty for labor costs.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; Emphasizes 'gradual' recovery, 'disciplined' execution, and 'measured' pricing; Confident in supply chain resilience vs. peers; Acknowledges near-term margin pressure but sees clear path to 14-15% EBITDA.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Cera temporarily shut one sanitaryware kiln in March/April to optimize gas costs while relying on built-up inventory, turning a cost constraint into a supply advantage vs. Morbi peers; INR 10cr Q4 profit boost from reversing over-provisioned wage code liabilities.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Established brand portfolio and pan-India distribution network cited as source of revenue resilience in a challenging demand environment
- Strategic gas-supply arrangement with GAIL enabled the Company to manage gas availability constraints and price spikes during the year by optimizing production planning
- Weighted average gas cost maintained below industry benchmark, cushioning input-cost volatility
- Robotic glazing technology gives more controlled, uniform glaze coating versus manual glazing and reduces dependence on manual labour
- First sanitaryware company in India to introduce 3D printers, considerably reducing concept-to-launch duration for new designs with improved aesthetics and symmetry
- Dedicated New Product Development (NPD) team with institutionalized knowledge-sharing platforms, structured review mechanisms and standardized operating procedures
- Newly commissioned state-of-the-art CNC router expected to accelerate product development cycles and improve dimensional precision
- Continuous-improvement manufacturing culture (Kaizen, waste elimination) cited as driving gains in resource utilization
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Economic risk — A slowdown in economic growth could reduce cash flows and profitability; management's mitigation cites India's projected fastest-growing-economy status with GDP growth of 6.8-7.2% in FY27.
- Regulatory risk — Stricter environmental regulations may demand heavy investments in new technologies or restrict operational capacity; mitigated per the Company via its compliance framework, proactive investments and employee training.
- Competition risk — Intensifying market competition could erode market position; mitigated per the Company through strategic investments in brand building, marketing, distribution and digital transformation.
- Fraud / internal-controls risk — Weak internal controls could expose the Company to fraud; mitigated per the Company via a stringent control system including centralized payments, dual authorization and enhanced financial oversight.
- Inflation risk — Rising inflation, if not fully passed on to consumers, could compress margins; mitigated per the Company through economies of scale, cost discipline and logistics efficiencies.
- Gas price / input-cost risk — Sustained increases in gas prices could weigh on profitability. During FY2025-26 gas availability was constrained and prices rose sharply; the Company managed this via its strategic supply arrangement with GAIL (optimizing production planning) and by maintaining a weighted average gas cost below the industry benchmark.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Sanitaryware 46% rev (+10.7% YoY, 70% util); Faucetware 43% rev (+24.3% YoY, 106% util); Tiles 9% rev (-8.3% YoY, fully outsourced); Wellness 2% rev (+31.2% YoY). Tier-3 cities 40% of sales.

outlook.body: FY27 Revenue growth 18-20% (Sanitaryware +12%, Faucetware +18%); EBITDA margin target 14-15%; Volume growth: Sanitaryware 7-8%, Faucetware 10-12%; Capex INR 43-45cr (includes INR 15cr office acquisition).
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Project business constitutes ~39-40% of revenue; pricing for projects locked for 1 year from booking, implying 5-6 month lag for recent 8-12% hikes to reflect; Retail prices effective immediately.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Senator (Premium) & Polipluz (Mass) targeting INR 70-80cr rev in FY27 (vs INR 19cr in FY26); Senator expanding to 60 flagship stores; Polipluz targeting 200 distributors/2000 dealers; Greenfield sanitaryware plant (land acquired INR 27cr) pending final investment decision.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Long-term growth strategy centred on a greenfield expansion project in the sanitaryware segment, to scale operations, adopt advanced manufacturing capabilities and capture emerging market opportunities.
- Continuous product development and design excellence via a dedicated New Product Development (NPD) team, with institutionalized knowledge-sharing platforms, structured review mechanisms and standardized operating procedures.
- Faucets business strategy of ongoing debottlenecking initiatives, adoption of advanced technologies, and increased automation of processes to drive further growth.
- Expanding colour/finish SKU portfolio in faucets (500+ colour SKUs) to align with changing customer preferences and market needs.
- Best-in-class manufacturing culture of continuous improvement (Kaizen principles, waste elimination) targeting resource-utilization gains, cost efficiency and sustainability.
- Faucets unit committed to focus on customer expectations while maximizing operational excellence.
- Dividend recommendations are governed by the Company's Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy (published on the Company's website); dividend declaration for the year is placed as an ordinary-business item for shareholder approval at the AGM. The Company also transfers a portion of profit to General Reserve each year as part of its retained-earnings practice.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: In line with its long-term growth strategy, the Company acquired a substantial portion of land for a greenfield expansion project focused on the sanitaryware segment, to scale operations and adopt advanced manufacturing capabilities. In the Faucetware unit, the Company completed an expansion to a total capacity of 5.2 million pieces per annum, alongside commissioning a world-class PVD colour facility (enabling colour-finish supply in under 15 days) and adding a new Electro Plating Line with copper-coating capability. The factory maintains Zero Liquid Discharge status and has added an 'Ozonater' effluent-treatment technology to further strengthen treatment capability. On the R&D/product-development side, the Company commissioned a state-of-the-art CNC router to accelerate product development cycles and improve dimensional precision, and continues to use robotic glazing and 3D printing technology in manufacturing. Separately, on the energy side, the Company has set up solar and wind plants with a combined capacity of 10.325 MW generating 13,163 MWh, meeting around 64% of its electricity requirement, and has installed a waste heat recovery system to optimize energy extraction from fuels.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India is expected to sustain strong growth at around 6.6% in FY27, underpinned by resilient domestic demand and structural advantages, positioning it as the fastest-growing major economy.
- India's sanitaryware industry is undergoing a structural shift toward design-led, water-efficient and space-optimized solutions, driven by rising incomes and evolving lifestyle aspirations.
- Organized players account for nearly 60% of the sanitaryware industry and are driving growth in the mass-premium and premium segments, while unorganized players continue to serve value-driven demand.
- Growth is increasingly concentrated in the mass-premium segment, where affordability intersects with aspiration, across both residential and commercial spaces.
- India's urban population is expected to nearly double from 48 crore in 2020 to 95 crore by 2050, sustaining demand for modern housing and commercial infrastructure.
- India's real estate sector, projected to grow from USD 532.6 billion in 2025 to USD 1.26 trillion by 2034 (10% CAGR), is amplifying demand for modern, eco-friendly, design-oriented sanitaryware.
- Government policy tailwinds cited: higher Union Budget FY27 capital expenditure (to Rs.12.2 lakh crore), Swachh Bharat Mission (Rs.7,192 crore allocation), AMRUT 2.0 (583 projects worth Rs.66,117 crore approved), PMAY (Rs.78,126 crore allocated in FY26, 122 lakh+ houses sanctioned) and the UDAN regional-connectivity scheme (Rs.550 crore) are all cited as demand drivers for specialized sanitaryware.
- Faucets business: Company expects even higher growth in the coming times, supported by new colour faucet designs launched in line with changing customer preferences.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Cera delivered 11.4% revenue growth in Q4FY26 driven by volume recovery (12%) and strategic price hikes, while leveraging Morbi's gas-driven supply disruptions to gain market share despite margin compression from brass costs. FY27 guidance of 18-20% revenue growth relies on sustained retail recovery, full realization of 12-16% price hikes, and scaling of new brands (Senator/Polipluz) to INR 70-80 crore.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Cera Sanitaryware is a 46-year-old, Kadi (Mehsana, Gujarat)-headquartered manufacturer and trader of sanitaryware, faucetware, tiles and bathroom accessories, positioned as one of India's fastest-growing home solutions providers across mass and luxury segments.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures and trades sanitaryware, faucetware, tiles and bathroom accessories & allied products, serving individual homeowners through a dealer/sub-dealer network and institutional customers (construction companies, real estate developers, government bodies) through direct engagement. It operates 2 plants and 33 offices/depots nationally across 28 states and 8 Union Territories in India, with exports to 16 countries contributing about 1% of turnover.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Packcart Packaging LLP — subsidiary: Was a 51%-owned subsidiary LLP; the Company divested its entire 51% stake on 29th September 2025, and it ceased to be a subsidiary with effect from that date.
- Race Polymer Arts LLP — subsidiary: Was a 51%-owned subsidiary LLP; the Company divested its entire 51% stake on 29th September 2025, and it ceased to be a subsidiary with effect from that date.
- Madhusudan Industries Limited — related party: Enterprise significantly influenced by Key Management Personnel and/or their relatives; counterparty in related-party transactions (e.g. purchase of goods).
- Cera Foundation — related party: Enterprise significantly influenced by Key Management Personnel and/or their relatives.
- Indian Council of Sanitaryware Manufacturers — related party: Enterprise significantly influenced by Key Management Personnel and/or their relatives.
- Madhusudan Gratuity Fund — related party: Post-employment benefit plan classified as a related party; recipient of contributions to the Gratuity Fund.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India is expected to sustain strong growth at around 6.6% in FY27, underpinned by resilient domestic demand and structural advantages, positioning it as the fastest-growing major economy.
- India's sanitaryware industry is undergoing a structural shift toward design-led, water-efficient and space-optimized solutions, driven by rising incomes and evolving lifestyle aspirations.
- Organized players account for nearly 60% of the sanitaryware industry and are driving growth in the mass-premium and premium segments, while unorganized players continue to serve value-driven demand.
- Growth is increasingly concentrated in the mass-premium segment, where affordability intersects with aspiration, across both residential and commercial spaces.
- India's urban population is expected to nearly double from 48 crore in 2020 to 95 crore by 2050, sustaining demand for modern housing and commercial infrastructure.
- India's real estate sector, projected to grow from USD 532.6 billion in 2025 to USD 1.26 trillion by 2034 (10% CAGR), is amplifying demand for modern, eco-friendly, design-oriented sanitaryware.
- Government policy tailwinds cited: higher Union Budget FY27 capital expenditure (to Rs.12.2 lakh crore), Swachh Bharat Mission (Rs.7,192 crore allocation), AMRUT 2.0 (583 projects worth Rs.66,117 crore approved), PMAY (Rs.78,126 crore allocated in FY26, 122 lakh+ houses sanctioned) and the UDAN regional-connectivity scheme (Rs.550 crore) are all cited as demand drivers for specialized sanitaryware.
- Faucets business: Company expects even higher growth in the coming times, supported by new colour faucet designs launched in line with changing customer preferences.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Q4 margin pressure from brass (+29% YoY) and trade discounts; Price hikes implemented: Sanitaryware +12% (retail), Faucetware +16% (retail) over 2 months; Still absorbing ~1-2% brass cost gap; Expect margin recovery via discount rationalization as demand stabilizes.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Cash balance INR 853cr; Dividend INR 75/share declared; Greenfield project (est. INR 130cr total, land done) under evaluation based on demand traction; No M&A announced.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: In line with its long-term growth strategy, the Company acquired a substantial portion of land for a greenfield expansion project focused on the sanitaryware segment, to scale operations and adopt advanced manufacturing capabilities. In the Faucetware unit, the Company completed an expansion to a total capacity of 5.2 million pieces per annum, alongside commissioning a world-class PVD colour facility (enabling colour-finish supply in under 15 days) and adding a new Electro Plating Line with copper-coating capability. The factory maintains Zero Liquid Discharge status and has added an 'Ozonater' effluent-treatment technology to further strengthen treatment capability. On the R&D/product-development side, the Company commissioned a state-of-the-art CNC router to accelerate product development cycles and improve dimensional precision, and continues to use robotic glazing and 3D printing technology in manufacturing. Separately, on the energy side, the Company has set up solar and wind plants with a combined capacity of 10.325 MW generating 13,163 MWh, meeting around 64% of its electricity requirement, and has installed a waste heat recovery system to optimize energy extraction from fuels.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic; Emphasizes 'gradual' recovery, 'disciplined' execution, and 'measured' pricing; Confident in supply chain resilience vs. peers; Acknowledges near-term margin pressure but sees clear path to 14-15% EBITDA.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Established brand portfolio and pan-India distribution network cited as source of revenue resilience in a challenging demand environment
- Strategic gas-supply arrangement with GAIL enabled the Company to manage gas availability constraints and price spikes during the year by optimizing production planning
- Weighted average gas cost maintained below industry benchmark, cushioning input-cost volatility
- Robotic glazing technology gives more controlled, uniform glaze coating versus manual glazing and reduces dependence on manual labour
- First sanitaryware company in India to introduce 3D printers, considerably reducing concept-to-launch duration for new designs with improved aesthetics and symmetry
- Dedicated New Product Development (NPD) team with institutionalized knowledge-sharing platforms, structured review mechanisms and standardized operating procedures
- Newly commissioned state-of-the-art CNC router expected to accelerate product development cycles and improve dimensional precision
- Continuous-improvement manufacturing culture (Kaizen, waste elimination) cited as driving gains in resource utilization

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Morbi gas supply normalization reducing Cera's relative advantage; Delay in trade discount rationalization; Brass/clay cost volatility exceeding price hikes; Tiles segment disruption due to outsourcing reliance on Morbi; Wage code settlement uncertainty for labor costs.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Cera temporarily shut one sanitaryware kiln in March/April to optimize gas costs while relying on built-up inventory, turning a cost constraint into a supply advantage vs. Morbi peers; INR 10cr Q4 profit boost from reversing over-provisioned wage code liabilities.

strategy.body:

- Continuous product development and design excellence via a dedicated New Product Development (NPD) team, with institutionalized knowledge-sharing platforms, structured review mechanisms and standardized operating procedures.

themes.title: Building-materials & home-improvement up-cycle
themes.need: The residential up-cycle pulls a broad finishing/home-improvement basket - tiles & sanitaryware (KAJARIACER/CERA/SOMANYCERA/ORIENTBELL/HINDWAREAP), wood-panels & laminates (CENTURYPLY/GREENPANEL/GREENLAM/RUSHIL/STYLAMIND), pipes/adhesives (PIDILITIND/SUPREMEIND/ASTRAL-tier) and paints (ASIANPAINT/CARYSIL/SIRCA). Premiumization + GST formalization shift share to organized players.
themes.driver: Festive/real-estate completion demand; GST 2.0 + commodity tailwinds; capacity commissioning and channel restocking.
